Why Did I Get Married? (2007)
Why Did I Get Married? follows four married couples who come together for their annual getaway, expecting a chance to relax, reconnect, and reflect on their relationships. But once everyone is together, personal issues, hidden frustrations, and questions about marriage begin coming to the surface. Each couple has a different relationship dynamic, giving the film multiple perspectives on love, communication, trust, and commitment. 

In pop culture, the film became one of the most recognizable relationship-centered Black movies of the 2000s. Created, written, directed by, and starring Tyler Perry, it featured a strong ensemble including Janet Jackson, Jill Scott, Malik Whitfield, Tasha Smith, and Richard T. Jones.

On a broader cultural level, Why Did I Get Married? opened up conversations about marriage, communication, infidelity, forgiveness, emotional needs, and maintaining relationships. Rather than presenting marriage as perfect, the film shows that even long-term relationships can have complicated problems behind closed doors.
